risk_plan.target_claim: Across all 28 fixed-seed guided-sim iterations spanning exogenous SOL/USD price shocks from 0 to 6000 bps (0% to -60%), every hard protocol solvency invariant held on the real tesoro_core.so and sim_lst.so binaries: vault LST balance covered open principal at every step, early unlock while debt remained rejected with Custom(6110) (DebtOutstanding), minted yield stayed strictly within the 2-month accrual bound (40,077,776 vs 116,763,898 lamports), and post-repayment unlock returned the full 10 simSOL principal. Crucially, Treasury share outlay for a 1,000-Gema fill_instant_redeem remained flat at 39,999,999 lamports (33.33% of the 0.12 simSOL seeded buffer) across the entire 0-60% SOL/USD crash because tesoro_core prices instant-redeem shares off the Source's locked issuance unit_num/unit_den rather than the post-shock spot PriceFeed — structurally insulating share-denominated Treasury reserves from post-issuance SOL/USD drops. This is evidence over the declared single-position, 2-month native-LST configuration only, not unconditional protocol safety.

surface.claim_boundary: This surface reports invariant-failure rates and metric percentiles observed within this campaign's declared, fixed-seed parameter region and run budget. It is evidence over that region only, not a proof of protocol safety or a prediction of mainnet behavior.

safe_region.message: Every populated cell stayed at or under the 5% failure-rate threshold within this declared, fixed-seed parameter region.

sensitivity.method: Per-axis marginal invariant-failure-rate spread: for each axis, the failure rate is computed per bin by marginalizing over the other axes (failed runs / runs in that bin), and the spread is max − min across that axis's populated bins. Axes are ranked by spread descending, ties broken by axis name ascending. The monotonic note compares consecutive populated bins by increasing bin index. The elasticity note is the signed average failure-rate change per bin step from the first to the last populated bin: (rate_last − rate_first) / (index_last − index_first); positive means risk rises with the axis.
